title: Cap. III Rat. 9: glory depending on others' sins needs foresight — Stephen's martyrdom
latin: Rat. 9. Quorum gloria dependet ex peccatis aliorum, iis non potest decerni nisi ex praevisione: ut verbi causa, quia gloria Stephani aliquo modo pendebat ex impietate Judaeorum qui illum erant lapidaturi, non potuit Deus gloriam illi decernere, saltem non in eo gradu quo tam glorioso martyrio danda fuit, nisi praeviso peccato quod occasionem praebebat ejus martyrio, et simul praevisa ejus patientia et fide quibus mediantibus ex illorum crudelitate eximiam martyrii gloriam sibi acquirebat. Si non omnibus ergo, at aliquibus saltem destinatur gloria ex praescientia meritorum.
pass_a: Reason 9. To those whose glory depends on the sins of others, it cannot be decreed except from foresight: as for example, because the glory of Stephen somehow hung upon the impiety of the Jews who were about to stone him, God could not decree glory to him, at least not in that degree in which it was to be given by so glorious a martyrdom, except with the sin foreseen which furnished occasion for his martyrdom, and at the same time with his patience and faith foreseen by which mediating from their cruelty he acquired for himself the outstanding glory of martyrdom. If not therefore to all, yet at least to some glory is destined from foresight of merits.
pass_b: Rat. 9. Where someone's glory hangs on others' sins, they say it cannot be decreed except from foresight. Take Stephen: his glory somehow depended on the impiety of the Jews who would stone him — so God could not decree him glory, at least not in the degree that so glorious a martyrdom would give, unless that sin (which occasioned the martyrdom) was foreseen, and with it his patience and faith, by which he won outstanding martyr's glory from their cruelty. So if not to all, at least to some glory is destined from foresight of merits.

title: Cap. III Sol. Rat. 9: intention vs execution — glory destined before foresight of faith
latin: Sol. Aliud est considerare gloriam ante jacta mundi fundamenta electis destinatam secundum Dei intentionem, aliud considerare eandem ipsis in tempore collatam per ejusdem decreti exsecutionem. In ipsa Dei intentione praedestinata fuit gloria, et tanta gloria Stephano, ante praescientiam patientiae et fidei ejus: Imo in praedestinationis decreto tantam fidem et patientiam Deus illi praeparaverat, quia ad tantam gloriam illum elegerat.
pass_a: Solution. It is one thing to consider glory destined to the elect before the foundations of the world were laid according to God's intention, another to consider the same conferred on them in time through the execution of the same decree. In God's intention itself glory was predestined, and so great a glory to Stephen, before foresight of his patience and faith: Nay, in the decree of predestination God had prepared for him so great a faith and patience, because he had elected him to so great a glory.
pass_b: Sol. One thing is glory destined to the elect before the world's foundations, according to God's intention; another is that same glory conferred on them in time by executing the decree. In God's intention itself glory — and so great a glory — was predestined to Stephen before foresight of his patience and faith. Indeed, in the decree of predestination God had prepared him that faith and patience because he had elected him to that glory.

title: Cap. III Sol. Rat. 9: in execution God foresaw cruelty, Stephen's constancy, the crown
latin: Sed in exsecutione hujus decreti Deus praevidebat Judaeorum crudelitatem, ipso permitente, martyrii occasionem Stephano praebituram. Praevidebat simul Stephanum tanta fide et constantia armatum cupide et libenter pro Christo moriturum. Praevidebat denique se, post certamen hoc tam praeclare certatum, eximiam coronam gloriae huic fortissimo militi donaturum.
pass_a: But in the execution of this decree God foresaw the cruelty of the Jews, himself permitting, that would furnish Stephen the occasion of martyrdom. He foresaw at the same time Stephen armed with so great faith and constancy about to die eagerly and willingly for Christ. He foresaw finally himself, after this combat so nobly fought, about to give an outstanding crown of glory to this most brave soldier.
pass_b: But in executing that decree God foresaw the Jews' cruelty — which he permitted — that would give Stephen occasion for martyrdom. He foresaw Stephen, armed with such faith and constancy, about to die eagerly and willingly for Christ. And he foresaw himself, after that fight so nobly fought, about to give this bravest soldier an outstanding crown of glory.

title: Cap. III Sol. Rat. 9: faith foreseen before obtaining crown, not before destinating it
latin: Praevisa igitur fuit fides et patientia Stephani ut antecedens ipsam coronae adeptionem; sed non fuit praevisa ut antecedens hujus coronae destinationem. Nam praescientia Divina de illa gratiae mensura quam largitus est Stephano, quamque ille exercuit tam gloriose, fundata fuit in praecedente decreto electionis; et non ipsum decretum electionis ad tantam gloriam, in praescientia fidei, quam accepturus a Deo et in certamine postmodum exseruit, fuit.
pass_a: Foresight therefore was had of the faith and patience of Stephen as antecedent to the obtaining itself of the crown; but it was not foreseen as antecedent to the destination of this crown. For the divine foresight of that measure of grace which he bestowed on Stephen, and which he exercised so gloriously, was founded in the preceding decree of election; and the decree itself of election to so great a glory was not [founded] in foresight of the faith which he was about to receive from God and afterward to display in the combat.
pass_b: So Stephen's faith and patience were foreseen as going before his actually receiving the crown — not as going before the destinating of that crown. Divine foresight of the measure of grace God gave him, and which he exercised so gloriously, rested on the prior decree of election; the decree electing him to that glory did not rest on foresight of the faith he would receive from God and later show in the fight.

title: Cap. III Sol. Rat. 9 close: can destine glory depending on others' sins without prior foresight to confer
latin: Falsum ergo fuit quod in argumento assumptum erat, nempe, non posse eam gloriam, quae aliquo modo dependet ex peccatis aliorum, decerni nisi ex tali praescientia. Decerni enim vel destinari potest, quamvis non conferri, nisi hujusmodi praescientia praeeunte.
pass_a: False therefore was what had been assumed in the argument, namely, that that glory which somehow depends on the sins of others cannot be decreed except from such foresight. For it can be decreed or destined, although it cannot be conferred, except with foresight of this sort going before.
pass_b: So the argument's assumption was false — that glory which somehow depends on others' sins cannot be decreed except from such foresight. It can be decreed or destined without that; it is only the conferring that cannot happen unless foresight of that sort goes first.
